meta.name: Microsoft Power Platform Functional Consultant Associate (PL-200)
meta.notes: Initial pack — 12 scenario-style questions across the PL-200 domains: Dataverse configuration, Power Apps (canvas + model-driven), Power Automate, Copilot Studio chatbots, security roles, environments and solution ALM, AI Builder, and Power BI integration. Correct-option positions distributed 3/3/3/3. v1.1: +10 — business rules, calculated vs rollup, duplicate detection, column security, environment variables, connection references, dataflows, public views, auditing, site map.

questions.question: A functional consultant is modelling a Dataverse table that must store the country of residence for each contact. The list of valid countries is known, small, must be the same across every form and view, and the choices must be re-usable on several other tables in the same solution. Which column type should they configure?
options: Choice column backed by a global choice (global option set) defined at the solution level
Single Line of Text column with a maxLength of 64 and an input mask
Local Choice column defined inline on the table, with options copied to each other table that needs them
Lookup column targeting a custom Country table populated with one row per country
questions.explanation: A global choice (formerly global option set) is defined once at the solution level and re-used by any Choice column on any table — exactly the requirement here. A Single Line of Text would accept any free-form value and lose validation. A local choice can only be used by the column it was authored on, so the options would have to be duplicated. A Country lookup table is heavier (extra rows, security and licensing implications) and is only justified when each value needs related data of its own.

questions.question: A field-service team needs a tablet app that lets technicians photograph equipment, capture a signature, work offline against a Dataverse table, and present a pixel-perfect, branded layout. Which Power Apps app type best fits these requirements?
options: Model-driven app, because it is automatically responsive and ships with offline support out of the box
Canvas app, because it gives pixel-level layout control and exposes device features such as Camera and Pen through Power Fx
Power Pages site, because it can be browsed from a tablet and supports anonymous external users
SharePoint list form customised with Power Apps, because it inherits the SharePoint mobile app's offline cache
questions.explanation: Canvas apps are the right choice when the scenario calls for pixel-level layout control plus device capabilities — the Camera and Pen controls expose photo capture and signature directly through Power Fx, and canvas apps support an explicit offline pattern (LoadData / SaveData / Connect). Model-driven apps follow the Dataverse form/view layout and do not give pixel-level control; Power Pages targets external-facing websites with anonymous or B2C audiences; SharePoint list forms cannot host the rich device controls or the offline pattern needed here.

questions.question: A consultant needs a Power Automate flow that runs every weekday at 06:00 local time, queries Dataverse for accounts that have no recent activity, and emails the owners. Which flow trigger should they choose?
options: Automated cloud flow triggered by 'When a row is added, modified or deleted' on the Account table
Instant cloud flow triggered by 'Manually trigger a flow', so a user can launch it each morning
Scheduled cloud flow with a Recurrence trigger configured for the right interval and time zone
Desktop flow recorded against the Dataverse web client and scheduled through Power Automate for desktop
questions.explanation: A Scheduled cloud flow starts from a Recurrence trigger, where the interval, frequency, time zone, start time and (for weekly schedules) the days of the week are configured — that is the canonical Power Automate pattern for a recurring server-side job. Automated flows react to a Dataverse change event, not a calendar; Instant flows need a human to start them; Desktop flows are intended for UI automation against a desktop or browser, not for a server-side query against Dataverse.

questions.question: A sales manager wants every opportunity to follow the same guided journey — Qualify, Develop, Propose, Close — with required fields surfaced on each step, the user able to see at a glance which step the deal is on, and the journey enforced consistently across model-driven app users. Which Power Platform feature should the consultant implement?
options: A Dataverse Business Rule with Recommendation actions on the Opportunity main form
A Power Automate cloud flow that runs on every Opportunity update and validates the current step
A Canvas app component library that renders a custom stepper bound to a Choice column
A Business Process Flow (BPF) defined on Opportunity, with one stage per phase and the required steps configured on each stage
questions.explanation: Business Process Flows are designed for exactly this scenario: a multi-stage, cross-form (and optionally cross-table) guided process with a visual stage indicator at the top of the form, required fields surfaced per stage, and a server-side enforced ordering. Business Rules apply form-level logic (set value, show error, recommend) but do not give a stage-by-stage journey. A Power Automate flow can react to updates but does not produce the in-form stage UI. A canvas component library cannot enforce process state on the model-driven Opportunity form for every user.

questions.question: A consultant is preparing to move a Power Platform customisation from a Development environment to Test and then Production. The customisation must be installable as a single, version-controlled unit that other teams cannot edit in the downstream environments. Which packaging approach should they use?
options: Author the changes in an unmanaged solution in Dev, then export the solution as managed and import the managed copy into Test and Production
Author the changes directly in Production's default solution so that no migration step is needed
Export each component (table, flow, app) individually using the Export to ZIP option, then import each file separately in Test and Production
Author the changes in an unmanaged solution and import the same unmanaged solution into Test and Production so that the components remain editable everywhere
questions.explanation: The recommended ALM pattern is to author in an unmanaged solution in the Dev environment (so components are editable), then export that solution as a managed solution and import the managed package into the downstream Test and Production environments. Managed solutions cannot be edited directly in the target environment and can be cleanly uninstalled, which gives the controlled, version-able deployment unit asked for. Working in Production's default solution loses ALM history entirely. Exporting components one-by-one is not a solution-based deployment and breaks dependency tracking. Importing the same unmanaged solution everywhere leaves the components editable in Test and Production, which contradicts the requirement.

questions.question: A consultant must grant a group of customer-service agents the ability to create and update Cases that they own, read Cases owned by other members of the same business unit, and read but not write Account rows. They must not be able to delete anything. What is the most appropriate way to implement this?
options: Assign each agent the system administrator role and document the policy in a SharePoint page that lists which actions they should avoid
Create a custom security role with Create/Read/Write on Case scoped to Business Unit, Read on Account scoped to Organization, no Delete privilege, and assign that role to the agents
Share each Case and Account row individually with each agent using the Share command in the model-driven app
Add the agents to a Microsoft 365 group and rely on Microsoft Entra ID group membership for table-level access, without configuring any Dataverse security role
questions.explanation: Dataverse security uses security roles that combine privileges (Create/Read/Write/Delete/Append/Append To/Share/Assign) with an access level (User, Business Unit, Parent: Child Business Units, Organization, or None). The right pattern is a custom role that grants Create/Read/Write on Case at the Business Unit level, Read on Account at Organization level, and no Delete privilege — then assigned to the agents. The system administrator role bypasses every restriction and cannot be locked down by documentation. Sharing rows one by one does not scale. Microsoft Entra group membership alone does not assign Dataverse privileges; a security role must always be assigned.

questions.question: A team is starting work on a brand-new customer-feedback solution. They want an isolated, non-production area where they can build and test without affecting the rest of the tenant, where they can reset the environment back to an empty state at any time, and which is clearly separated from the default environment created with the tenant. Which type of environment should they create?
options: Default environment — every user already has Maker access, so iteration is fastest
Developer environment — but only after each maker has separately signed up for their own personal developer plan
Sandbox environment — non-production, can be reset, copied or restored, and is governed by the same ALM controls as Production
Production environment with the 'low-cost' setting, since sandbox environments do not support Dataverse
questions.explanation: A Sandbox environment is the purpose-built non-production environment in Power Platform: it can be Reset (wiping all data and configuration back to an empty state), Copied from a Production environment for testing, and is fully governed by the same ALM tools (solutions, deployment pipelines) as Production. The default environment is shared by the entire tenant and is not isolated. Developer environments are personal and one-per-user, not the shared team workspace described. Sandbox environments fully support Dataverse — the 'production-only Dataverse' statement is incorrect.

questions.question: A Dataverse data model has an Account table and a Contact table. Each Contact must belong to exactly one Account, while an Account can have many Contacts. The Contact form should display the parent Account, and deleting an Account should also delete its Contacts. Which type of table relationship should the consultant configure between Account and Contact?
options: A Many-to-many (N:N) relationship with the default Referential, Restrict Delete cascade behaviour
Two separate One-to-many (1:N) relationships — one from Account to Contact and one from Contact to Account — to model the bidirectional navigation
A self-referential One-to-many relationship on the Contact table, using a Parent Contact lookup
A One-to-many (1:N) relationship from Account (one) to Contact (many), with the lookup column placed on Contact and a Parental cascade behaviour on the Delete event
questions.explanation: The scenario — one parent on the many side, with the parent's deletion removing its children — is a textbook One-to-many relationship. The lookup column lives on the many side (Contact) and points back to the parent (Account). To make deletion of the parent remove its children automatically, the relationship's cascade behaviour for Delete is set to Parental (or the wider 'Parental' configuration preset). A many-to-many relationship would let one Contact belong to many Accounts, which contradicts the scenario. Two separate 1:N relationships duplicate the model and do not enforce the parent/child rule. A self-referential 1:N on Contact does not link Contact to Account at all.

questions.question: Purchase requests in a Dataverse table must be approved by the requester's manager before processing. The approval must be visible in Outlook, in the Power Automate mobile app, and in Microsoft Teams, and the approval record (approver, decision, comment, timestamp) must be queryable later for audit. Which approach should the consultant take?
options: Build the flow on the Approvals connector — Start and wait for an approval — and act on the response in the subsequent branch
Send a plain email through the Office 365 Outlook 'Send an email' action and parse the reply text to detect 'Approve' or 'Reject'
Embed a custom HTML form in a SharePoint list and use a daily scheduled flow to scrape the responses
Create a model-driven app form for the manager and require them to update an Approval Status choice column by hand
questions.explanation: The Power Automate Approvals connector ('Start and wait for an approval' / 'Create an approval' + 'Wait for an approval') is the canonical pattern. Approvals automatically surface in the approver's inbox in Outlook, in the Power Automate mobile app, in Microsoft Teams, and on the Approvals page — and every action is recorded in Dataverse so the approver, decision, comments and timestamps are queryable. Parsing free-form email replies is fragile and not auditable. SharePoint HTML scraping is not a supported pattern. Asking the manager to manually edit a choice column gives no audit trail and no multi-channel UX.

questions.question: A consultant needs to surface an interactive Power BI report inside a model-driven app's main dashboard so that users see live data filtered to the row they have selected, and so that filters set inside the model-driven app pass through to the report. Which integration should they configure?
options: Export the report to PDF on a schedule with Power Automate and attach the latest file to the dashboard as a Note
Embed the Power BI report on the model-driven app dashboard as a Power BI tile/report component, and configure contextual filters so model-driven app selections pass through to the report
Take screenshots of the report from Power BI Desktop and upload them as web resources on the dashboard, refreshing them weekly
Add an iframe web resource that points at app.powerbi.com without enabling cross-frame communication
questions.explanation: Model-driven app dashboards natively support Power BI embedding — both Power BI report and Power BI tile components — and the embedded report can be configured with contextual filters so a record selected in the model-driven app passes the right context to the report. PDFs attached as notes are static and do not support live drill-down. Screenshots are static and stale almost immediately. A plain iframe to app.powerbi.com without the supported Power BI dashboard component loses authentication context, contextual filters and the supported embedding APIs.

questions.question: A consultant is building a customer-support chatbot in Microsoft Copilot Studio (formerly Power Virtual Agents). They want the bot to respond to questions about 'shipping costs' whether the user types 'how much is delivery', 'what does shipping cost', or 'do you charge for postage'. Which authoring construct in Copilot Studio handles this requirement?
options: A scheduled trigger that fires once a day and broadcasts the answer to every connected channel
A Power Automate cloud flow that intercepts the message at the channel level and decides which topic to call
A topic whose trigger phrases include several natural-language variations of the same intent, so the bot's natural-language understanding routes any of them to the same conversation node
A Dataverse business rule that, when triggered by an inbound message, sets the bot's response field on the Chat Session table
questions.explanation: In Copilot Studio (formerly Power Virtual Agents), the unit of authoring is a topic, and each topic has a list of trigger phrases. The natural-language understanding model learns from those phrases so a single topic answers many paraphrases of the same intent. Scheduled triggers are not how user messages route. A Power Automate flow can extend a topic but is not how the inbound classification is done. Business rules apply to Dataverse columns, not to chatbot intent classification.

questions.question: A consultant must process scanned supplier invoices that arrive as PDFs. The bot needs to extract supplier name, invoice number, line items and total, including from layouts it has not seen before. They want to start fast, ship a working pilot in days, and only build a custom model later if accuracy is not enough. Which AI Builder model should they use first?
options: A custom Object Detection model trained on a small set of cropped logos so the supplier name is read first
A Form Processing custom model trained on five sample documents per layout, retrained whenever a new layout arrives
A custom Category Classification model on the email body that routes the message to the right team before any extraction is attempted
The Invoice Processing prebuilt model, which is pre-trained to extract the standard invoice fields and line items from invoice PDFs without any training data
questions.explanation: AI Builder ships a set of prebuilt models that are already trained for common document types — Invoice Processing, Receipt Processing, Identity Document Reader and Business Card Reader — and can be called from Power Apps or Power Automate immediately, with no training data. For an invoice scenario where the goal is to ship fast and only escalate to a custom model if accuracy falls short, the Invoice Processing prebuilt model is the right starting point. Object Detection, custom Form Processing and Category Classification all require labelled training data and are heavier than necessary for the initial pilot.

questions.question: On the Case form, the 'Refund amount' column must become required and visible only when 'Case type' equals 'Refund' — with the logic also enforced in the mobile app, without code. What does the consultant create?
options: A business rule on the Case table with a condition on Case type and actions to show and require the column
An OnChange JavaScript handler registered on the Case type column of the main form
A real-time classic workflow that updates a hidden flag column on the Case record, which the form then reacts to after the user manually refreshes the page
A duplicate of the main form per case type, assigned to different security roles
questions.explanation: Business rules are the no-code way to apply form logic — show/hide, require, set values, validate — based on conditions, and they run consistently across web, mobile and (with entity scope) server-side. JavaScript is code; a workflow plus hidden flag is a fragile workaround; per-type forms multiply maintenance and role assignment doesn't switch forms by data value.

questions.question: Two requirements: (a) a 'Days open' column computed from Created On and today's date on each Case; (b) a 'Total open cases' count on the parent Account. Which Dataverse column types satisfy (a) and (b)?
options: A rollup column for 'Days open' and a calculated column for the count on Account
A calculated (formula) column for 'Days open' and a rollup column for the Account count
Two Power Automate flows writing both values into standard columns every fifteen minutes
Two rollup columns, since rollups handle both same-row math and child aggregation
questions.explanation: Calculated/formula columns derive a value from the same row's data (date math like DIFFINDAYS) and evaluate on read; rollup columns aggregate child rows related to a parent (COUNT of open Cases per Account) on a system-managed refresh schedule. Rollups can't do same-row formulas and calculated columns can't aggregate children; flows would work but are unnecessary machinery with refresh lag.

questions.question: Service agents keep creating Contact records that already exist. The consultant must warn agents when they save a Contact whose email matches an existing one — in the standard UI, without blocking legitimate saves. What should be configured?
options: A synchronous classic workflow that deletes any new contact whose email already exists in the table
Column-level security on the email column so only data stewards can populate it during creation
A Dataverse duplicate detection rule on Contact email, published and enabled for create and update
A validation business rule that compares the email against a static list maintained by the admin team
questions.explanation: Duplicate detection rules generate matchcodes and surface a non-blocking warning dialog when a save matches — the agent can review and proceed or open the existing record. Auto-deleting records destroys data; column security restricts access, not duplication; business rules can't query other rows for matches.

questions.question: Only the payroll team may see the 'Salary' column on the Employee table — all other users with read access to Employee rows must see the column masked, including in views, search and the API. How is this achieved?
options: Remove the Salary column from every form, view and search layout so it is no longer rendered anywhere in the user interface of the app
Enable column security on Salary and grant read through a column security profile assigned to payroll
Move salary data to a separate unrelated table that only payroll's app surfaces in its navigation
Create a payroll-only form containing the column and assign other roles a form without it
questions.explanation: Column-level security secures the column itself: enabling it denies access by default and a column security profile grants read/update/create to specific teams or users, enforced at the platform layer — forms, views, Advanced Find and the API all respect it. Hiding from forms/views or splitting tables is presentation-level and leaks through search and API access.

questions.question: A solution moving between Dev, Test and Prod calls an external API whose base URL differs per environment. Admins must set the value at deployment time without editing the flow or app. What should the consultant add to the solution?
options: An environment variable referenced by the flow and app, with its value supplied per environment
A dedicated Dataverse configuration table holding one settings row per environment that administrators remember to update manually after every import
Three branches of the flow guarded by conditions on the environment's display name string
A connection reference renamed per environment so the URL travels with the connection metadata
questions.explanation: Environment variables are the solution-aware configuration mechanism: definitions ship in the solution, values are provided per environment (at import or later), and flows/apps reference them symbolically. A config table works but isn't ALM-integrated (no import-time prompt, manual step every deploy); name-sniffing branches are brittle; connection references carry credentials/connections, not arbitrary settings.

questions.question: After importing a managed solution into Test, its cloud flows are off and a banner asks for missing dependencies tied to the connectors the flows use. What solution component prevents this and lets flows activate with Test's own connections?
options: An on-premises data gateway registered in the Test environment and shared with the deployment service account before the import runs
A custom connector exported separately and installed by hand ahead of each deployment
A service principal granted the Environment Maker role inside the Test environment
Connection references included in the solution and bound to Test connections at import
questions.explanation: Connection references decouple flows from specific connections: the solution ships the reference, and at import (or first turn-on) an admin binds each reference to a connection that exists in the target environment, letting all flows activate cleanly. Gateways serve on-prem data sources only; custom connectors define APIs, not bindings; maker-role service principals don't resolve connector bindings by themselves.

questions.question: Product data must be pulled from an external SQL database into Dataverse every night, with transformation (column renames, type fixes, merges) applied before load — maintained by a functional consultant, not a developer. Which tool fits?
options: A dataflow using Power Query to transform and load into Dataverse tables on a schedule
An SSIS package using a third-party Dataverse adapter, deployed and scheduled on an Azure virtual machine maintained by the integration team
A desktop flow that opens the legacy database client and re-keys changed rows nightly
The classic Data Import Wizard run from a CSV the DBA exports manually each evening
questions.explanation: Dataflows bring Power Query's low-code transformation surface into Power Platform: connect to SQL, shape the data, map to Dataverse tables, and refresh on a schedule. SSIS is developer/infrastructure tooling; a desktop flow re-keying rows is RPA misapplied to a structured source; the import wizard is for one-off manual loads, not scheduled transformed ingestion.

questions.question: Sales reps need a list in the model-driven app showing only THEIR open opportunities closing this quarter, with specific columns, available from the view selector. What does the consultant create?
options: A dashboard with a single grid component for opportunities, pinned as the app's default landing page for every member of the sales team
A new public view on Opportunity with filter criteria (owner = current user, status, close date) and chosen columns
A personal view built in one rep's account and shared by them to the whole sales team
A canvas app embedded on the opportunity form that queries Dataverse with FetchXML
questions.explanation: Views define filtered, sorted column lists for a table; a public (system) view with 'equals current user' on owner plus status/date criteria appears in everyone's view selector and behaves per-user. Personal views depend on one user maintaining and sharing them; dashboards aggregate views rather than define them; an embedded canvas app is heavy machinery for a list definition.

questions.question: Compliance asks who changed the 'Credit limit' value on a specific Account three weeks ago, including old and new values. Nothing was configured in advance beyond default settings. What does the consultant explain, and what should be set up going forward?
options: The plug-in trace log already captured the change; enabling tracing today retroactively decodes the older entries, including old and new values for the credit limit column
Solution history shows the change because credit limit edits are treated as customizations
Dataverse auditing must be enabled (org, table and column level) — it only records changes made after activation, so the past change is unrecoverable
The column's rollup refresh history stores prior values for ninety days by default
questions.explanation: Dataverse auditing records create/update/delete with old and new values, but only once enabled at the environment level plus on the table/columns concerned — it cannot reconstruct changes made before activation. Plug-in traces log code execution, solution history logs customization imports, and rollup refresh does not version data. Enable auditing now to answer such questions in the future.

questions.question: A model-driven app must gain a new navigation area called 'Quality' containing the Inspections table and an embedded dashboard, visible only within this app. Where is this configured?
options: In the app designer's navigation (site map) editor, adding the area, group and subarea entries
In each user's personalization settings, pinning the Inspections table to their navigation rail
Through a security role granting the Inspections table, which auto-inserts it into navigation
By adding the Inspections table to the solution, which appends it to every app's navigation
questions.explanation: An app's navigation is its site map, edited in the app designer: areas, groups and subareas pointing at tables, dashboards and pages — scoped to that app only. Security roles control access but never add navigation entries; solution membership doesn't touch any app's map; personal pinning is per-user and not an admin-managed structure.
